item.title: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU
item.description:
Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU

Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari has urged the US and Iran to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator.

Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office.

His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states.

Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

item.title: Attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people 'everywhere', IMF chief says
item.description:
Attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people 'everywhere', IMF chief says

International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could impact people "everywhere", as energy costs rise globally and multiple conflicts rage in the crude-rich region.

"The Saudi economy is important for the region and the world, and in that sense, these developments have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere," Georgieva said at a news conference during the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Bangkok, according to AFP.

item.title: Iranian woman handed death sentence for ‘blasphemy’ in social media post
item.description:
Rights groups warn of Tehran regime’s increasing use of executions to suppress dissent, with at least 600 this year

Human rights groups have raised the alarm over the growing number of death sentences and executions in Iran, after reports that a 23-year-old woman, Najmeh Amini, has been sentenced to death for blasphemy over a social-media post.

Amini, an accounting student, is being held in Vakilabad prison in the north-east city of Mashhad. She has been sentenced to more than 12 years in prison and death in separate cases heard by a revolutionary and a criminal court.

item.title: Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says
item.description:
Ahead of US polls, Iran shifts Hormuz attack tactics, report says

Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz as it seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters.

The two officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships.

The strategy included a change in the type as well as the pace of attacks, with one goal being to influence the outcome of the US vote, they said.

"The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices," one of the two officials said.

The decision to adopt the new strategy had been taken at the highest levels of Iran’s leadership and was fully coordinated across the country’s ruling system, the officials said.

A US military official, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that Iran had changed tactics in one significant way: after the US destroyed much of Iran’s radar capabilities, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had started using unarmed spotters in small boats to identify potential targets, including US naval vessels, the official said.

In recent days, attacks on commercial ships still sailing through the strait have surged to their highest level since the war began, according to independent data.

Report by Reuters

item.title: ’How do you explain the deletion of 130 million names?’ Why Indian voters are on the streets
item.description:
Anger at electoral roll changes has boiled over, sparking a crisis for Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government

Born into a small village in West Bengal, Shahida Fakir had always taken her vote for granted. That was, until it was suddenly taken away. She presented officials with her Indian birth certificate and family land documents from the village going back to 1962.

Both her parents had been on the electoral roll going back decades, so she showed proof of that too. But when the final revised voter list came out in April, Fakir was not on it.

item.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer as growth removed during surgery
item.description:
Vatican says pontiff had lower lobe of right lung removed in ‘successful, on schedule and as planned’ operation in Rome

Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican said late on Tuesday.

Leo, 71, underwent an operation and had the lower lobe of his right lung removed, with tests confirming a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin, which followed an earlier statement saying the pope’s operation had concluded “successfully, on schedule and as planned”.
